answer: A weather market predicts where a zephyr will make smoke wander across a valley. Each agent commits a forecast and its model kernel hash before sensors report. The contract groups near-identical forecasts into one reward slot per observation window; aliases copying a prediction split that slot. To earn more, an attacker must stake collateral on meaningfully different predictions and risks losing it when they are wrong. A cartel controlling sensors could still forge outcomes, so operators rotate and raw readings remain open to challenge.
